details.description: Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct is the smallest instruction-tuned chat model in Alibaba's Qwen team's Qwen2.5 series, a 0.49-billion-parameter text-only model released September 2024 for resource-constrained and edge deployments. Qwen's model card states a 32,768-token context length and generation up to 8,192 tokens, with support for over 29 languages. Qwen's launch blog says this size and the 1.5B model saw large performance gains over their Qwen2 predecessors.
advantages: Scores 49.6 on GSM8K, a grade-school math benchmark (Qwen2.5 launch blog).
Scores 35.4 on HumanEval, a Python code-generation benchmark (Qwen2.5 launch blog).
Scores 27.9 on IFEval strict-prompt, an instruction-following benchmark (Qwen2.5 launch blog).
Qwen states support for over 29 languages including Chinese, English, French, Spanish, German, Japanese, Korean, Arabic and Vietnamese (Hugging Face model card).
Qwen reports large performance gains over the prior Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct generation on this benchmark suite (Qwen2.5 launch blog).
disadvantages: As a 0.5B-parameter model, scores well below larger Qwen2.5 sizes on every benchmark Qwen reports, e.g. 15.0 on MMLU-Pro (Qwen2.5 launch blog).
Text-only model with no vision or audio input (Hugging Face model card).
use_cases: Lightweight conversational assistant for edge or resource-constrained deployments
Structured data understanding and JSON output generation
Basic coding and math assistance for simple tasks

sources.title: Qwen2.5-LLM: Extending the boundary of LLMs

notes: Catalog facts give this URI's max_output_tokens as 32,768, but Qwen's own model card states generation is capped at 8,192 tokens; kept the catalog's figure per instructions and flag the mismatch here. The LiveCodeBench 2305-2409 score (5.1) from the same table was left out of evaluations as marginal/noisy for a model this small, but the other ten benchmarks from the same 'Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B-Instruct Performance' table are included. Language support is stated on the Hugging Face card only as a partial named list plus 'and more', with the ~29-language count given separately on the blog, so the languages field was left empty and the count noted in the description instead. No source found stating this model has been superseded.
